away.headline: Two new players land on Pitt injury report vs. Virginia Tech
away.blurb: Defensive end Zach Crothers and tight end Elijah Lagg have both been listed as doubtful to play against the Hokies. Receiver Tony Kinsler has been upgraded to probable after being tabbed as questionable on Wednesday. Safety Cruce Brookins is still questionable to suit up. Two new players have popped up on the availability report for Pitt on Thursday night ahead of Friday night’s clash with Virginia Tech in Blacksburg. Panthers head coach Pat Narduzzi isn’t thrilled that his team has to deal with another short week before an ACC matchup, after previously beating Syracuse on a Thursday earlier this season. “I wish we didn’t have two short weeks (for) two ACC games,” Narduzzi said on Wednesday in his office at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. “When you talk about conference play, it’s most important, and our first two games are short weeks and different weeks. I think it certainly helps us (having played) on a Thursday night. Although the schedule’s totally different, I think it does help us play in a mid-week game.” Both teams enter the primetime matchup at 4-0, but neither are ranked. There is also an undercurrent with James Franklin and Narduzzi having been painted as adversaries since the former’s time at Penn State.

Greene is one of the top receivers for offensive coordinator Ty Howle, and Franklin is also anticipating him to be back on Friday night, per Bitter . Now, there are still four days until the kickoff time against Pitt approaches, and things can certainly change. Trailing 14-6, the Hokies scored on back-to-back drives late for their first ACC win under James Franklin. The short week means everything moves up a day, including gameday to Friday night, when Virginia Tech hosts Pittsburgh in a battle of two 4-0 teams at Lane Stadium . Coaches want every possible advantage they can get before game day arrives, so handing out information on which of their players could or could not play is somewhat of an immediate disadvantage, because it lets the other team plan accordingly, and personnel is everything in football. In the latest student-athlete availability report for Boston College football's first conference game of the season, which is against Virginia Tech on Saturday in the wake of an impending Nor'easter that could bring heavy winds and sideways rain to Chestnut Hill, Mass., the Eagles have a relatively high number of injuries entering the contest, the majority of which are categorized as fully "out." The players in that category who were just recently injured would be tight ends Brady Clough and Bryce Lewis, defensive back Cameron Martinez, linebackers Bodie Kahoun and Justin Medlock , and defensive tackle Chris Marable Jr., all of whom played in BC's first two games of the year before sitting out against Maine last Saturday. Now in the "doubtful" category is defensive back Syair Torrence, who is slowly making his return from a season-ending injury he sustained just two games into his redshirt-freshman campaign last year. "It's all about health," O'Brien said of the reason he played mostly on special teams. "He's one of our best players. It has nothing to do with anything other than his health. Whether it was coming back from the knee, which was a serious knee injury, or some soft-tissue stuff he's dealing with. But yeah, once he's really 100 percent healthy, he'll [be out there]. He practiced today, so we'll see how it goes for Saturday." On the bright side, defensive end Kris Jones - one of the best pass rushers on the team - is listed as "questionable," and defensive lineman Onye Nwosisi is in the "probably" category. Nwosisi made his season debut last week against Maine and totaled three tackles and two quarterback hits, so his availability is quite massive. away.headline: Penn State-Northwestern Thursday injury reports: What are the top takeaways 24 hours before kickoff?
away.blurb: Penn State and Northwestern both put out their final Big Ten weekday availability reports before game day on Thursday night. What did we learn about Matt Campbell’s and David Braun’s teams 24 hours before the Nittany Lions clash with the Wildcats at 8 p.m. ET Friday on FOX? Starting with the visitors, top cornerback Daryus Dixson is still questionable. The second-year Nittany Lion appeared on Tuesday’s first report of the week as questionable. Speaking Wednesday morning, Campbell said that would be the case on that night’s report, and it indeed was. Beyond that, there is no other new news for the Lions. Kickoff specialist Cristiano Rosa is out and will not travel to Evanston. Lucas Tenbrock or Ryan Barker will handle kickoffs. Cornerback Christian Askew and linebacker Cam Smith are in the same boat. Top tight end Luke Dehnicke is now doubtful for the Wildcats. He’s a key part of their offense, so it’s obviously not good news for Northwestern. No. 2 receiver Hayden Eligon II is now probable, which is good news, of course. Top defensive back Braden Turner , who did not play last week, is also now doubtful as well. Another key cornerback, Josh Fussel , is now out. Another defensive back to monitor, Damon Walters , is now doubtful for Friday’s game. Last but not least, defensive tackle Troy Regovich could return to action. He is questionable. For those confused, the conference requires teams to put one of these out starting three days before game day. Most weeks, that will be Wednesday-Friday for head coach Matt Campbell’s team before a Saturday game. However, since this contest is Friday at 8 p.m. ET on FOX, the reports started on Tuesday. The final one then comes out two hours before kickoff. Northwestern is calling top tight end Luke Dehnicke questionable. The same goes for No. 2 receiver Hayden Eligon II and two of the team’s top tacklers, defensive backs Braden Turner and Damon Walters . More notable is that one of the team’s top corners, Josh Fussell , is doubtful to play. The Wildcats look likely to be shorthanded in the secondary this week. “[He] got dinged up right at the end of the first half [against Wisconsin],” Campbell said on Wednesday. “Kind of fought through it. Played. I thought he did a really good job. Then he was really, really sore, banged up here early in the week. So I think we’ll kind of see where he’s at. He was on the practice field today.” Penn State-Northwestern matchups: Who will have the edge on Saturday at the new Ryan Field? As for Northwestern, the Wildcats will be shorthanded Friday night. away.blurb: Coaches want every possible advantage they can get before game day arrives, so handing out information on which of their players could or could not play is somewhat of an immediate disadvantage, because it lets the other team plan accordingly, and personnel is everything in football. In the latest student-athlete availability report for Boston College football’s first conference game of the season, which is against Virginia Tech on Saturday in the wake of an impending Nor’easter that could bring heavy winds and sideways rain to Chestnut Hill, Mass., the Eagles have a relatively high number of injuries entering the contest, the majority of which are categorized as fully “out.” The players in that category who were just recently injured would be tight ends Brady Clough and Bryce Lewis, defensive back Cameron Martinez, linebackers Bodie Kahoun and Justin Medlock, and defensive tackle Chris Marable Jr., all of whom played in BC’s first two games of the year before sitting out against Maine last Saturday. Now in the “doubtful” category is defensive back Syair Torrence, who is slowly making his return from a season-ending injury he sustained just two games into his redshirt-freshman campaign last year. “It’s all about health,” O’Brien said of the reason he played mostly on special teams. “He’s one of our best players. It has nothing to do with anything other than his health. Whether it was coming back from the knee, which was a serious knee injury, or some soft-tissue stuff he’s dealing with. But yeah, once he’s really 100 percent healthy, he’ll [be out there]. He practiced today, so we’ll see how it goes for Saturday.” On the bright side, defensive end Kris Jones — one of the best pass rushers on the team — is listed as “questionable,” and defensive lineman Onye Nwosisi is in the “probably” category. Nwosisi made his season debut last week against Maine and totaled three tackles and two quarterback hits, so his availability is quite massive. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/bostoncollege as Boston College Football Injury Report: What Stands Out Ahead of Virginia Tech? . While the ACC’s student-athlete availability reports, which the conference introduced last season, aim at putting together an accurate injury report for every league matchup of the season for football, men’s and women’s basketball, and baseball, they often aren’t the most telling of where players who are listed on them actually stand — especially in football. With that being said, there is still obviously some truth to them. Georgia Southern is ready to turn the page. The Eagles enter Sun Belt play at 1-3 after dropping three straight games, including Saturday’s 42-28 loss to No. 25 Houston at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Despite the loss, Georgia Southern showed some encouraging signs offensively. Quarterback Max Johnson turned in his strongest performance of the season, completing 26 of 38 passes for 284 yards and a season-high three touchdowns without an interception. The Eagles also continued to expand the role of quarterback Weston Bryan. Georgia Southern used packages featuring both quarterbacks on the field together, including a flea-flicker that started with Bryan and ended with Johnson finding Alex Taylor for a 40-yard touchdown. Taylor finished with a season-high 119 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Southern now turns its attention to conference play while also dealing with several injuries. Head coach Clay Helton confirmed Monday that wide receiver Ashton Hollins will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery. Hollins, an Illinois transfer, suffered the injury in the Eagles’ loss at Jacksonville State. Inside linebacker Rashon Myles Jr. also left Saturday’s game against Houston with an Achilles injury. Helton said Myles was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday to determine the extent of the injury. The Eagles were also without two starting offensive tackles against Houston because of illness. Helton said neither had been medically cleared to play. Georgia Southern will now look to regroup as the Sun Belt portion of its schedule begins. The Eagles have lost three straight, while Coastal Carolina enters the matchup at 1-3 and riding a two-game losing streak. Both teams now look for a fresh start, 0-0 in conference play. Saturday will also mark Georgia Southern’s first matchup against the Chanticleers under first-year Coastal Carolina head coach Ryan Beard. The Eagles have won three straight games in the series, including a 26-6 victory in their last trip to Conway in 2024. Georgia Southern leads the all-time series 8-4.
